Read a dictionary file

Source: R/dict.R
read_dict.Rd

read_dict() reads a dictionary file, checks every entry against the schema (see dict_file) and returns a weft_dict: a named list of the values, in file order. In a knit weft reads dict.yml at the project root itself and puts the result in the document as dict (rule 4.1.1), so read_dict() is for use outside a knit.

Usage

read_dict(path = "dict.yml")

Arguments

path

One string naming an existing file.

Value

A weft_dict, with the attributes file, scope ("project" or "local"), entries (a data frame of the keys' type, definition, unit, decision, why, line and display), registered and local_keys.

Details

Units a quantity names that the units package does not know are installed with units::install_unit() as the file is read, for as long as that project's configuration stays in force (rule 4.4.7); a unit already known is not installed again. A read that reports a problem installs no unit. The attribute registered holds the units the dictionary needs that udunits does not ship, whenever and by whomever they were installed, so two reads of one file give the same registered, and print() lists them.

The units installed are removed when another project's configuration is read and by units_reset(), so a unit one project's dictionary declared is not known to the next project's document (decision 63). In a knit, dict and dict_local are removed at the start of every top-level knit and assigned again from that knit's own files: a document with neither sees neither, and an object of the session's own called dict is replaced during a knit that has a dictionary and is not restored.

dict$key and dict[["key"]] match the key exactly: a key not held is a weft_dict_key_error, never NULL (rule 4.1.2). A dictionary is read-only (rule 4.1.4): assigning to it, names<- and dict[...] are a weft_dict_error. str(), summary(), lapply(), Map() and mapply() work on it as they do on the plain list; attr<- and class<- cannot be stopped. as.list() gives the plain named list of values.

All the problems in a file are collected and raised together as one weft_dict_error. A chunk served from knitr's cache that read dict is not re-run when dict.yml changes.

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
writeLines(c("min_samples:",
             "  value: 5",
             "  type: number",
             "  definition: Fewest samples a site needs."), f)
d <- read_dict(f)
d$min_samples
#> [1] 5
